scenes.heading: Sensors
scenes.narration: Sensors are special Airflow tasks that pause a workflow until an external condition becomes true.

scenes.heading: What sensors watch for
bullets: A file landing in cloud storage.
A partition appearing in a table.
An external job or API reaching completion.
scenes.narration: Sensors commonly wait for a file to arrive before processing it. They can also block until a table partition is ready or an upstream job finishes. Some simply hold until a scheduled time window opens, ensuring tasks only run when their inputs truly exist.

scenes.heading: Poke vs reschedule mode
scenes.narration: In poke mode a sensor keeps its worker slot and checks repeatedly, which is fine for quick waits. In reschedule mode it releases the slot between checks and requeues itself, avoiding wasted resources during long waits. Choosing reschedule mode for lengthy dependencies keeps your cluster from clogging.

scenes.heading: A file sensor gating a load
scenes.code:
from airflow.sensors.filesystem import FileSensor

wait_for_file = FileSensor(
    task_id="wait_for_drop",
    filepath="/data/incoming/orders.csv",
    mode="reschedule",   # free the worker between checks
    poke_interval=60,
    timeout=60 * 60,
)

wait_for_file >> load_orders
scenes.narration: This sensor checks every minute for the orders file and gives up after an hour. Reschedule mode releases the worker between checks so it does not tie up capacity. Only once the file appears does the downstream load task begin, guaranteeing it never runs on missing input.

scenes.text: Sensors pause a workflow until a condition holds, and reschedule mode keeps long waits from wasting worker capacity.
scenes.narration: Use sensors to make pipelines react to reality, starting work only when the data it needs has actually arrived.
